# Finite multi-time kinetic energy observations

**Type:** bounded_theorem

Claim type: bounded_theorem

This is a positive conditional theorem in the supplied massive free CAR
vacuum model. It gives every fixed ordered word of bounded energy unitaries
and the joint probabilities of a specified finite Lüders energy-measurement
protocol. The two conclusions have different classical interpretations.
The canonical mathematical cores below are unchanged source slices.

    target_claim_type: bounded_theorem
    actual_current_surface_status: conditional-support
    trace_class: upstream_support

Ordinary analytic acceptance is the exact multi-time root acceptance
`d7211e292bee2d461b4c50d65f25b10cf8ccec83ca121c2844af430a9c959638`
and its root review `57fd843917f99b2619ea03e4be7c40a3d8bf92a12e642b10af4d6f6bace382dc`.
This assembly supplies no new independent derivation, retained audit,
formal certificate, physical-model identification or empirical prediction.
The two derivations and later comparison share parent machinery and the
selected model family. Their different overlap and squeeze arguments are
identified below; agent count is not evidence of model diversity.

The result uses fixed real compact smooth spatial slots, positive mass and
velocity, a fixed kinetic horizon, the free vacuum, and fixed finite lists
of observation times, spectral parameters and bins. Real amplitude and
frequency profiles have the stated fixed supremum and total-variation
budgets; the frequency stays in a compact interval strictly above `2m`.
For constant frequency, the independently frozen proof below derives the
finite-word and lattice-bin theorem. For a chirped profile, composition uses
the separately accepted exact V2/850 parent estimates. That composition is
source-exposed use of accepted premises, not an independent new chirp check.

Writing `M(du,de)=(pi/2)a(u)^2 r(varpi(u)) du delta_varpi(u)(de)`, the
auxiliary bosonic Weyl representation gives the complete ordered-word
formula in root T14–T17. Chronological words have the marked compound-Poisson
increment characteristic function T18. General orders can have different
limits, as the explicit root late/early commutator and independent
three-time example show. The bosonic representation is a representation of
these limiting moments; the microscopic field statistics remain CAR.

For the actual specified finite Lüders protocol, root T19–T21 prove joint
bin probabilities by bounded spectral calculus. Every finite boundary in
the root theorem avoids the point spectrum of the auxiliary total energy
`K=dGamma(e)`. The constant-carrier proof separately permits the first
half-line bin to include zero while avoiding positive lattice boundaries.
The comparison's gap-based zero-boundary extension is reproduced as a
distinct third core. None of these sufficient conditions classifies every
atomic endpoint. No bin-convergence rate or path-space theorem is claimed.

For conditional cell transfer the representations must have the **exact
same selfadjoint H0, vacuum and Lüders projections**. The two generators are
`H0+lambda c_h V` and `H0+lambda c_h V_ell`, with the same scalar drive, and
`||V_ell-V|| <= d0 epsilon_ell`. With `h=|lambda|`,
`delta_h=d0 epsilon_ell A tau_star/h`, a fixed N-factor unitary word changes
by at most `2N delta_h`; a fixed n-observation joint history probability
changes by at most `4n delta_h`. Thus `epsilon_ell=o(h)` suffices for these
bounded protocols. An energy-mean identification or an isometric embedding
alone would not identify the measurement instrument. This statement does
not compare normalized states after arbitrarily rare postselection.

Unmeasured single-time means and W1 remain separate inherited results.
Their transfer retains the common energy/vacuum, bounded control error,
bounded commutator forms on `D(H0)`, the commutator-error estimate, and the
resolvent work identity of the accepted parents. The stronger sufficient
scale is `epsilon_ell=o(h^2)`. Neither that scale's necessity nor mean/W1
after sequential collapse is proved by the bounded history theorem.
